card.problem: Intraday buy-and-hold on the NIFTY front future (09:21 to 15:15) earns about 0.2bp a day overall, but it loses on calm days: when the previous close of India VIX is below about 14, the average session return is around -1.9bp, and when VIX is above 14 it is around +2.6bp (my quick split over 2022-2026, not a result).
card.motivation: The reference row loses most of its edge in low-VIX regimes. If the session drift is pay for bearing intraday variance, it should only show up when variance is priced high. Being long only on those days would cut the reference's losing days without adding any new signal.
card.approach: Run the buy-and-hold reference only on sessions where the previous day's India VIX close is above a threshold, and stay flat otherwise.
card.plan: Copy specs/refs/buy_hold.yaml and add a vix feature with entry long: m == 5 and v > p.vthr. Keep the same session, wide stop and sizing. Run CPCV on the research window with a grid of vthr = [12, 14, 17], which are the VIX quartile edges in data/vix for 2022-2026.
card.mechanism: When VIX is high, hedgers and leveraged longs de-risk into the open and overnight, and whoever takes the other side of that flow during the session is paid a variance premium. In calm regimes nobody pays that premium, and option-writer delta hedging plus retail long unwinds pull the session flat to slightly negative.
card.rule: long at 09:21 if m == 5 and vix > p.vthr; exit 15:15 or stop_atr 50

vthr.source: Median previous-day India VIX close 2022-2026 in data/vix, which is where the sign of the buy-and-hold session mean flips in my quartile split (Q1 -1.6bp, Q2 -2.2bp, Q3 +3.0bp, Q4 +2.2bp)

kill: CPCV median path Sharpe <= the ref_buy_hold Sharpe over the same window
The sign flips in more than 2 of the 5 calendar years 2022-2026 (VIX above the threshold gives a negative mean session return)
The result disappears after dated costs (cost ratio fails)

messages.author: judge
messages.body: judge prefers h2 over h1: Simplicity: B has one param, no new rules (it reuses the reference's exit and stop) and every number has a source, while A adds a 1 ATR stop with no source. A has the better mechanism (named option-writer counterparty), but B's kill criteria are checkable against a named reference and the VIX threshold is the one weakness (read off the same data it will be tested on), so it should be treated as a fitted number. No past cards, so novelty does not separate them.

messages.author: verifier
messages.body: spec matches card. It's the buy-and-hold reference plus the VIX gate. Features minute_of_day and vix are both on the whitelist. The vix feature is already lagged to the previous day's close, so no same-day look-ahead. The rule m == 5 is the 09:20 bar (minute_of_day counts from 09:15), filled at 09:21, as the card says. vthr is 14 and the grid is 12/14/17, centred on the frozen value. Stop, exit and sizing match the reference. I didn't check the scripted checks (look-ahead probe, determinism, fallback lint); I only saw "schema ok".
